story.who: Three of the four artists whose films make up the programme: Ayo Akingbade (The Fist, 2022), Maz Murray (Principal Boy, 2024) and Gaby Sahhar (a 2026 film). The gallery's own website says all four have taken part in its Participation Programme in recent years, each building a new joint project alongside Duchamp & Sons, its youth collective.
story.started: Part 2 follows Part 1, shown in spring 2026, in a film series for the gallery's 125th anniversary.
story.then: Part 1 drew on interviews, archive footage and analysis of artists' work, with figures including Barbara Hepworth, David Hockney, Frida Kahlo and Philip Guston, according to the gallery's own website.
story.now: This second instalment turns to artists connected to the gallery's recent history. The gallery's own website says the films explore identity, place, memory and resistance, and reflect on personal and collective histories and the politics of belonging.
worth_knowing: It is the second instalment of a screening series marking the gallery's 125th anniversary.
Ayo Akingbade's The Fist runs 24 minutes and Gaby Sahhar's Abstraction Belongs to Us runs 12.

evidence.quote: These four artists have all contributed to Whitechapel Gallery’s Participation Programme in recent years. Each one worked closely with our youth collective, Duchamp & Sons, to develop a new collaborative project.
